column1: # Mutant batch for most-recently-used browse ordering in the snippet picker.
#   scripts/mutate.sh batch scripts/mutants/snip-mru.tsv
# Tab-separated: NAME <TAB> FILE <TAB> FROM <TAB> TO [<TAB> TEST_FILTER]
# FROM must occur EXACTLY ONCE in FILE or the mutant is refused. Every FROM
# below was checked for single occurrence before the row was written.
# 🔴 DEFINITIONS ONLY, NEVER RESULTS. A verdict is void the moment the tree
# moves — see scripts/MUTATION-TESTING.md. The verdicts these produced live in
# the pull request for this change, stamped with the commit they were measured
# on.
# 🔴 WHY THIS BATCH CARRIES MORE WEIGHT THAN USUAL. This change has NO
# regression coverage and cannot have any: SnipUsageStore arrives with it, so a
# run at the base commit is a compile error rather than a test watched going
# red, and the feature's behaviour cannot even be expressed at base (asserting
# "browse is ordered by use" requires being able to record use). Every test is
# therefore an invariant guard. These mutants plus the partial-revert control
# recorded in the PR are the ONLY evidence those guards can go red at all.
# 🔴 The partial-revert control is NOT in this file and is not a substitute for
# m-mru01: it deletes the whole filterRows body, which m-mru01 does more
# narrowly. It is recorded in the PR because it is the control a reader can
# reproduce without the harness.
# 🔴 FOUR SURVIVED ON THE FIRST RUN (fd43127), splitting two ways. The verdicts
# live in the PR; what belongs HERE is which rows are EXPECTED to survive a
# re-run, so the next reader does not re-investigate them.
#   m-mru03, m-mru07 — REAL COVERAGE GAPS, now closed, and they must NOT
#     survive again. m-mru03 deletes the browse gate so ordering leaks into
#     typed queries; the test written for exactly that could not see it,
#     because its query matched ONE row and a one-row list is identically
#     ordered under every sort. m-mru07 moves the never-used sentinel to 0L,
#     which no fixture could distinguish because every stamp was >= 1000.
#     Killed by tests added after that run:
#     aTypedQueryMatchingSeveralRowsKeepsRankOrderAndIgnoresUsage and
#     aNeverUsedRowSortsBelowEvenAZeroStamp.
#   m-mru09, m-mru19 — UNREACHABLE GUARDS, EXPECTED to survive. Their survival
#     is not a missing test. m-mru09's empty-liveLabels case cannot be reached
#     through the activity (a row is only pickable after readRows populated the
#     set); m-mru19's branch runs only when renameTo FAILS, which it does not on
#     the test filesystem. Both are documented at their call sites with this
#     verdict, so neither reads as covered code. Deleting either would be
#     defensible; both are kept because what they prevent is losing the
#     operator's entire usage file.
# 🔴 m-mru03 is the one that matters most and the reason the batch exists.
# SnipUsageOrderTest and SnipUsageStoreTest both stay GREEN under the
# partial-revert control — they test the pure function and the store, neither
# of which the picker's wiring touches. That is the "verified in isolation"
# seam: two components each covered, the defect living in the seam nobody owns.
# m-mru03 mutates the GATE between them.
